title: Character Entropy in Modern and Historical Texts: Comparison Metrics for an Undeciphered Manuscript
summary: The authors compile three public corpora: Voynich texts stratified by transcription, Currier variety and scribal hand, Wikipedia samples in 294 languages, and 18 historical texts in eight languages. They use these corpora to estimate conditional character entropy and examine the contribution of transcription choices and word-position constraints.
established: The study reports first-order conditional character entropy of 2.159 bits for full Voynich in Maximal EVA and 2.475 bits in the Minimal representation. Changing the representation moved the estimate, while comparison with the corpora still highlighted unusually tight restrictions on where frequent symbols appear within tokens.

In the three tested representations, Appendix A reports lower conditional character entropy for Currier B than for Currier A. The historical comparisons examine paired diplomatic and normalized transcriptions to assess the effect of abbreviation and orthography.

open.question: Can a historically motivated encoding that collapses sound distinctions reproduce the low conditional entropy and the associated pattern of strongly position-restricted bigrams?
open.check: Use a fixed encoding rule and matched-length historical texts. Compare the entropy and position-stratified bigram profiles jointly under more than one Voynich glyph representation.
